title: Type look: subtle idle motion that makes it feel alive
description:
Add 3 subtle always-on motions to the Type look, inside the RD-02 policy, so it feels alive while open. The maintainer wants calm, not flashy.

Do:
- Caret breathes: opacity 0.6 to 1.0 on a 2 s cycle, in its own box after the last word; it never moves the text.
- Baseline grid pulses with the level: grid alpha 4 % at rest, up to 7 % with the smoothed level.
- Ink sheen: once every 12 s a 1 s sheen crosses the status word. (The plan said the last word; that is on the reading line, so it moves to the status word.)
- Run through the RD-02 paced idle path at its capped rate, only while the popup is open; stop at once on exit and on a look switch. Nothing changes the glyphs of the newest line.
- Reduced motion (`reduced-motion` or VO_REDUCED_MOTION=1): all of them off, the look still.
Files: src/bin/osd_vo/type_look.rs.

Acceptance (B = target/release/voxtype-osd-vo built through heavy-build with `--features osd-vo`; D = a new empty folder):
- Given type open with no speech, when the RD-02 per-look measurement runs, then idle frames stay at or under the capped rate. CPU and GPU stay under the RD-02 budget (proposed: 2 % of one core, 1 ms GPU per frame at 600x300).
- Given `B --theme type --offline D --moment long-silence`, when two idle-tail frames 1 s apart are compared (`compare -metric AE`), then some panel pixels differ and none inside the newest line's box (newest_line_centre +/- half a line).
- Given the same run with VO_REDUCED_MOTION=1, then those two frames are identical.
- Given done and cancel (`--offline D --cancel`), then the run exits 0 and no "still moving" in stderr.
- Given the look chord steps away while idle, then the old idle loops stop in that frame.
- `B --theme type --envelope` adds no breach with the idle motion on.
Tests: the checks above; the RD-02 number for this look goes in docs/REDESIGN-PLAN.md.

title: EDIT M7.2 Proxy lifecycle
description:
WHY: Popup editing inside each look own layout (shared edit layer plus per-look adapters).  Plan id M7.2, v1.

FILES: src/bin/voxtype_osd_vo.rs, src/bin/osd_vo/edit_focus.rs

WHAT TO DO: Proxy lifecycle. Implement exactly the acceptance below; plan section 6 row M7.2 and the sections it cites are the spec.

REQUIREMENTS (quoted in full):
- R3 (v1): Focus is taken through a separate Overlay layer surface with `on_demand`, mapped with a buffer attached. The visible popup stays at `KeyboardInteractivity::None`. The reason is that KWin's `handleAcceptsFocusChanged` has no branch for the switch back to false, and an `on_demand` popup would steal focus every time it is mapped [V]. This is recorded in `INPUT-MODEL.md`.
- R5 (v1): On a `leave` the popup did not request, the state becomes Detached. "Requested" means a flag the popup sets before it destroys the proxy. Lock screen, output removal, click-away and Alt+Tab all lead to Detached. A single Right Shift tap re-enters editing with the same buffer and caret. Focus is never taken back by itself.
- R6 (v1): On `leave`: cancel repeat, clear logical key state, and cancel any pending compose sequence. No later key releases are expected. Destroying the proxy does not wait for a `leave` event.
- R40 (v1): From the single-tap decision (release + `double_tap_ms`) to the caret shown takes at most 100 ms [G, measured in M0.1 and M7.2]. With 300 ms that is at most about 400 ms after the release.
- R41 (v1): From key to pixels: the first presented frame after a key shows the change. Measured with the presentation-feedback frame log.

ACCEPTANCE (machine-checkable): Nested KWin: R3, R5, R6 and R40. Detached and re-enter work.

TESTS REQUIRED: add the tests that prove each acceptance sentence (unit, golden or nested-KWin as fits), run through heavy-build, and report the exact commands and pass counts in the close reason. Security or paste-safety changes need a regression test.

DEPENDS ON (plan): M1.3, M7.1

- Repos: ~/work/voxtype on branch voxtype-onnx-isolation; ~/work/voxtype-osd-gpu (the vo framework, paths prefixed vo:) on main. Read each repo's CLAUDE.md first.

title: ASR-08 Evaluate Nemotron streaming 0.6B as the live model
description:
Why: cache-aware streaming with 80 to 160 ms chunks and no 12x re-encode; parakeet-rs already has model_nemotron.rs. Would put the popup at 160 to 300 ms.

Do:
- Get the ONNX export parakeet-rs expects (the model card and parakeet-rs docs), int8 if available; models go under ~/.local/share/voxtype/models/.
- Same LibriSpeech eval as ASR-07 at 80, 160 and 560 ms chunks: WER, commit wait, CPU per second of audio, peak RSS. Check it exposes the same per-step signals (ASR-02 style).
- If it wins on latency within 0.5 % WER and fits memory (the maintainer's main criterion; today's live worker peaks at 1.4 GB), add it as a live_preview_model option, but do not switch the default without the maintainer.
Files: voxtype live-preview model plumbing (src/transcribe/), eval under /var/tmp/claude/asr/ASR-08/.

Acceptance: the eval table; an option that runs live in the worker, or a written reason it does not fit.

Context: research page https://claude.ai/artifact/PNRjafNcUxBTuTuqvci9uq; scripts, data and plots in /var/tmp/claude/asr-internals/ (probe_stream.py is a Python port of the parakeet-rs unified loop that reproduces the offline transcripts exactly; surgery.py exports encoder layers; sweep.py the window sweep). Live model: parakeet-unified-en-0.6b-int8, plain RNN-T, 1025-way joint (blank = 1024), steps every 0.56 s over a window of 5.6 s left + 0.56 s chunk + 0.56 s right context, greedy, append-only; median commit wait 0.96 s. parakeet-rs fork: github.com/oysteinkrog/parakeet-rs branch voxtype-confidence (f250ecc), checked out in ~/src/parakeet-rs; never edit there: add a worktree under /var/tmp/claude/ on a new branch voxtype-signals off voxtype-confidence, commit there, and the lead pushes it and moves voxtype's [patch] in Cargo.toml to a rev. voxtype code: ~/work/voxtype (worker.rs, subprocess.rs, revisions.rs, osd/live.rs, the popup). Privacy: the maintainer's own recordings and transcripts stay local; results from them go only to ~/work/life/setup/voxtype/. Public repos get no private words or /home paths. Swarm rules: /var/tmp/claude/fxlib/swarm/RULES.md (heavy-build, debug builds, commit with a pathspec, never push). Heavy jobs (over 2 GB or 4 cores, GPU training) run as `systemd-run --user --slice=builds.slice --scope nice -n 10 <cmd>`.
close_reason: Does not fit: Nemotron streaming 0.6B int8 on the ASR-07 subset (437 LibriSpeech test-clean utts) is +0.71 pp WER at 560 ms (2.60 % vs 1.88 %, CI +0.43..+1.02), +0.91 at 160 ms, +1.08 at 80 ms; all over the 0.5 % rule. Waits 0.08/0.16/0.48 s vs 0.88 s. Peak RSS ~1.45 GB vs 1.49 GB (same harness). 80 ms needs 96 % of real time at 4 threads. parakeet-rs Nemotron lacks the live APIs (timings, confidences, details, frame signals, flush, chunk size). No option added. Eval in /var/tmp/claude/asr/ASR-08/.

title: R2-15 Bioluminescent: Breathing Membrane, Prism Light, Ink Reveal
description:

- Breathing Membrane (R2-15-a):
  - What: three layered closed paths with noise wobble grow with the voice; tendrils sway.
  - Driver and place: smoothed RMS. Around the bubble and text; tendrils stay inside the popup.
  - Subtle: layer alpha 20 % or less. Reduced: still membranes.
  - Uses: paths; EG-13 for the tendrils.
- Prism Light (R2-15-b):
  - What: soft god rays through the bubble and a rim hue band with a few glints; fades out over 600 ms on finish.

  - Subtle: ray alpha 12 % or less. Reduced: still hue band.
  - Uses: gradient cones or vo-3d light cones; no EG.
- Ink Reveal (R2-15-c):
  - What: ink clouds swirl around and behind the text, fed at the newest word's box; wisps drift away.
  - Driver and place: word-commit and RMS. Behind the text; ink alpha at the newest line 20 % or less.
  - Subtle: one hue. Reduced: still ink wash.
  - Uses: EG-11, EG-12.

- Given idle-open and recording, then the RD-02 log shows idle at 30 fps or less, CPU under 2 % of a core, GPU p95 under 1 ms at 600x300.
- Given a full dictation and a cancel, then the RD-05 exit check passes.

- Given `--motion reduced-motion`, then the moments show each reduced form above.
- Human check: the maintainer approves a recorded clip of one dictation (`--record`, played with `--preview --replay`).

Tests: Membrane scale is a pure function of RMS; rays are 0 after 600 ms of finish; the fluid replays to the same snapshot. Rendering one moment twice gives identical frames.

title: EG-08 Effects can leave the popup: automatic margins and a fly-out layer
description:
Size: M. Gap cards: 2.

Why: glows and motion get cut at the surface edge. vo already sizes a transparent margin from `Scene::effect_reach` (`SurfaceMargin::Auto`, crates/vo/src/lib.rs), but only from the first view (crates/vo/src/live.rs, `start_inner`), so an effect that starts later, such as an exit streak, is clipped. Big exits (a text card flying to the app, long streaks, a reflection below the popup) also need room far outside the popup.

Do:
- Margins that follow the show: when a later view reaches further than the current margin, grow the surface (mid-show resize exists) without moving the panel on screen; shrink back once the effect settles. Keep a small hysteresis so the surface does not resize every frame. The margin never shrinks below the first view's.
- A fly-out layer: an element can ask to draw on a short-lived full-screen click-through surface (`InputMode::None`, on the popup's output) for big exits. It opens when the element needs it and closes when the element settles or at the exit cap (EXIT_MOTION_MAX), whichever is first. It uses the existing multi-surface support (crates/vo/src/surfaces.rs; the popup's captions look uses several surfaces).
- Reduced motion: a fly-out element ends in place (fade), so no fly-out surface opens.
- In the popup, switch one look (swiss) from its hand-set surface size to the automatic margin as the example. Other looks adopt it in their own beads.
Files: crates/vo/src/live.rs, crates/vo/src/surfaces.rs, crates/vo-scene/src/reach.rs; src/bin/voxtype_osd_vo.rs (swiss `surface()` only) in the popup.

Acceptance:
- Given a vo test app whose view adds a glow of radius 40 px at t = 1 s, when its driver runs (unit test, no display), then `Scene::clipped` is zero at every frame, and the main surface is larger only while the glow shows.
- Given an exit card that flies 800 px up, then a fly-out surface opens, the card is never clipped (`clipped` zero on that surface), and the surface closes within EXIT_MOTION_MAX of the exit.
- Given VO_REDUCED_MOTION=1, then no fly-out surface opens.
- Given the popup idle with no effect showing, then its surface size equals the first view's size (logged), and no extra surface is open.
- Given swiss, when `voxtype-osd-vo --envelope --theme swiss` runs, then it exits 0, and `--exit-check --theme swiss` (RD-05, if landed) exits 0.

title: EDIT M5.4 Pause and resume handlers, `record edit` CLI

description:

Do:

  - What: particles flow in from the left along a curl field and form the newest word behind it, then disperse in 500 ms.

title: EG-01 Backdrop capture: render the layers under an element into a texture
description:

Why: ripples that bend (EG-03), refracting glass (EG-05), layer blur and frost (EG-04), water reflections (EG-10) and text on surfaces all need the pixels under an element. Today no element can read what was drawn before it.

title: RD-01 Each look turns on its own motion set by default
description:
Why: the everyday popup shows almost none of the 73 motion exhibits. Features turn on only through `--motion` or VOXTYPE_OSD_VO_MOTION, and the daemon passes neither. This bead gives each look a default motion set, so each look runs the effects its redesign chose.

Do:
- New src/bin/osd_vo/defaults.rs with `pub(crate) fn defaults(theme: OsdTheme) -> &'static [&'static str]`. Fill the rows of the 20 existing looks from docs/REDESIGN-PLAN.md section 3 (backticked names only; built-in effects need no entry). End the match with `_ => &[]`, so the 7 new looks (RD-03) need no edit here; each new look's FX bead adds its own row.
- `Look::on` (src/bin/voxtype_osd_vo.rs) also answers true for `defaults(self.theme)`, unless the resolved motion setting is `none`. Read `self.theme` at call time, never a list resolved at startup, so a look switch with the look chord mid-show uses the new look's set.
- Config `[osd] motion` in src/osd/config.rs: `"look"` (default, the look's set), `"none"` (no defaults, today's behaviour), or a list of names. A list with any plain name replaces the set; `no-<name>` removes a name; a list of only `no-` entries means the look's set minus those. CLI `--motion` and VOXTYPE_OSD_VO_MOTION win over the config and follow the same rules (`--motion none` works). Missing field = `"look"`; an unknown name is ignored, never an error.
- Station exhibits (`--station`) keep exactly their own features, as if motion were `none`, so each exhibit still shows one effect. `--wall`, `--offline` and `--envelope` use the look's set.
- `reduced-motion` (feature or VO_REDUCED_MOTION=1) leaves the set on; each effect draws its reduced form as today.
- docs/CONFIGURATION.md: document `[osd] motion` next to `look_chord`, with the per-look sets and the opt-out.
Files: src/bin/osd_vo/defaults.rs (new), src/bin/voxtype_osd_vo.rs, src/osd/config.rs, docs/CONFIGURATION.md.

Acceptance:
- Given theme swiss and no motion config, when `Look::on` is asked, then it is true for pause-marks, pitch-baseline, audio-ruler and fold-under, and false for onset-ink.
- Given `[osd] motion = "none"`, then `Look::on("fold-under")` is false for swiss.
- Given `--motion onset-ink` on swiss, then only onset-ink is on.
- Given `motion = ["no-fold-under"]` on swiss, then the other three defaults are on and fold-under is off.
- Given a swiss Look whose theme changes to amber (look chord), then `on` answers amber's set.
- Given a station exhibit, then `on` is true only for that exhibit's features.
- Given every look in OsdTheme::VO_LOOKS, when `voxtype-osd-vo --envelope --theme <look>` runs, then it exits 0, also with `--cancel` and with VO_REDUCED_MOTION=1. Log the per-look GPU p95 it prints.

title: R2-11 Cyberpunk glitch: Luminous Ink Flow, Breathing Focus Field, Typewriter Horizon
description:
Why: Cyberpunk has glitch and neon. Round 2 adds smoke ink, a breathing contour field and a typewriter platen, all kept off the reading line. Design: /var/tmp/claude/fxlib/redesign2/11.png.

Do:
- Luminous Ink Flow (R2-11-a):
  - What: a smoke stream flows in from the left behind the newest word; a ghost copy of the word in the smoke dissolves over 600 ms.
  - Driver and place: word-commit and RMS. Behind and left of the word.
  - Rule: the design dissolves and sharpens the word itself; here the word is sharp at 70 % ink or more from its first frame and only the ghost dissolves. Reduced: no stream, ink rise only.
  - Uses: EG-11, EG-12.
- Breathing Focus Field (R2-11-b):
  - What: faint concentric contour lines behind the text drift outward; the frame inset breathes 4 px or less.
  - Driver and place: RMS sets phase speed and inset. Background and frame; the text is never scaled.
  - Subtle: line alpha 12 % or less. Reduced: still contours, fixed inset.
  - Uses: a WGSL material; no EG.
- Typewriter Horizon (R2-11-c):
  - What: a platen roller with knobs below the text turns a notch per word; a carriage marker glides to the newest word's x; paper grain and a typewriter font.
  - Driver and place: word-commit. Below the text.
  - Rule: the design moves the paper and text; here the text stays still. Reduced: marker jumps, roller still.
  - Uses: EG-28; grain is a procedural material.

title: RD-09 follow-up: synthwave and cyberpunk move the newest line while the card grows
description:
Found in RD-09 (voxtype-osd-gpu-fgaw). Maintainer decision needed; no envelope limit was changed.

Both looks keep the card's bottom edge fixed and grow it upward when the text wraps. The text hangs from the card's top, so the whole block, newest line included, moves up a line over the growth. The code says this is deliberate (cyberpunk.rs: 'a new line rises from behind the bar while the panel grows').

title: EG-03 Displacement pass: ripples, noise and curls bend a layer
description:
Size: L. Gap cards: 3.

Why: the only distortions today are CRT curvature, glitch slices, chromatic split, perspective warp and motion blur. Sonic ripples, liquid echoes and ink smears need a layer redrawn with each pixel moved by a field.

Do:
- A displacement pass: redraw a captured layer (EG-01) with each pixel offset by a source. Sources: expanding ripple rings seeded by events (closed form in t, so they replay), noise and curl fields (the existing WGSL noise), a page-curl cylinder, and a texture of offsets (any texture; EG-10 later feeds it water heights, this bead tests it with a synthetic texture).
- API on elements or layers, for example `Element::displace(Displace::Ripples { .. })`; strength animatable and bindable to a signal.
- The newest (reading) line is exempt by default: a mask keeps it sharp and still, so the reading-line envelope holds. An explicit opt-out exists for text that is not read.
- Reduced motion: displacement strength 0 (the layer draws as captured, no pass cost).
- Add effect_cost cases `displace ripples` and `displace noise`.
Files: crates/vo-render/src/displace.rs and wgsl/displace.wgsl (new); crates/vo-scene/src/element.rs, display.rs.

Acceptance:
- Given a demo with a waveform and an older text line under two ripple rings from onsets at t = 0.2 and 0.5 s, when rendered offscreen at t = 0.8 s, then it matches a new golden in crates/vo-render/tests/gpu_displace.rs, and the reading line's pixels equal the same scene without displacement.
- Given the texture source with a constant offset of (3, 0) px, then the output equals the input shifted 3 px (within golden tolerance).
- Given VO_REDUCED_MOTION=1 or strength 0, then output equals the undisplaced layer, byte for byte.
- Given the same demo rendered twice, and once with a seek back from t = 1.5 s to 0.8 s, then frames at equal t are byte-identical.
- Given each other source (noise, curl, page curl) on the same layer, then each matches its own golden.
- Given the demo through `vo::envelope::check_scenario`, then it passes.
- Given effect_cost at 600x300, then each displace case adds under 2 ms; numbers in the commit message.
Tests: gpu_displace.rs goldens; `just test`, `just test-gpu`, `just budget` exit 0; a vo example or vo-preview demo.

title: EG-09 Water surface simulation
description:
Size: L. Gap cards: 5.

Why: water designs (rings from each word, a pool under the text) need a real wave surface with memory, which closed-form ripples cannot give. vo has no field simulation today.

Do:
- A height-field wave simulation (wave equation with damping) on a GPU grid, as a `Sim` of crates/vo-sim (EG-00): fixed 120 Hz tick, events with timestamps, snapshots, `state_at(t)`.
- Drops are events: from word onsets and voice level (the caller turns signals into recorded events; the sim never reads live audio directly), each with position, radius and strength.
- Output a height texture and a normal texture that EG-10 (shading) and EG-03 (texture displacement) can sample.
- Grid size is a parameter; default low (for example 128x64 for a 600x300 popup). Document GPU cost per tick and snapshot memory.
- Reduced motion: drops are ignored and the surface stays flat.
- Stable at any frame rate: the tick count at t depends only on t.
Files: crates/vo-sim/src/water.rs and crates/vo-sim/src/wgsl/water.wgsl (new); crates/vo-sim/tests/gpu_water.rs (new).

Acceptance:
- Given two drops 40 cells apart at t = 0 and 0.1 s, when the state is read back at t = 0.6 s, then the height midway between them shows constructive interference (larger than either single-drop run at that point, within tolerance), and the max |height| at t = 4 s is under 5 % of its peak (damping).
- Given the same events, when sampled through frame steps of 1/144 s and of 1/60 s, then the height textures at the same t are byte-identical.
- Given a seek back from t = 5 s to t = 2 s, then the state equals a fresh run to 2 s.
- Given VO_REDUCED_MOTION=1 (or the sim's reduced flag), then heights stay 0.
- Given the default grid at 600x300, then GPU time per tick plus the normal pass is under 0.3 ms (timestamp queries; skipped without them), number logged.
Tests: crates/vo-sim/tests/gpu_water.rs for the cases above (run by `just test-gpu`); `just test`, `just lint` exit 0; a vo-preview demo or vo example that shows the height field as grey, with drops from a scripted onset list.

title: EG-31 Backgrounds that know where the words are
description:
Size: M. Gap cards: 17.

Why: a background cannot react to where words are. The jump-flood text field (`TextField`, crates/vo-3d/src/field.rs) exists but only vo-3d's `Stack` uses it, and vo-render cannot depend on vo-3d.

Do:
- Move `TextField` and field.wgsl into crates/vo-render/src/text_field.rs; re-export from vo-3d so its API and tests stay.
- Material inputs: `text_dist(px) -> vec4f` (signed distance in pixels, direction away from ink, coverage) through the EG-02 texture binding, and a word table (up to 64 word rects with word id and age in seconds) with `word_near(px)`.
- Built only when a material in the list asks for them (a flag on the material), at half resolution as today, and only when the text changes; zero cost otherwise.
- Reduced motion: age is treated as settled, so the lift shows without a rise.
- Demo: 23 'Breathing Grid' contours brighten and lift (shading only, materials cannot move geometry) around each new word, in material_demo.

Tests: unit tests for the word table; GPU tests above at scale 1 and 1.5 and light mode.

title: R2-06 Phosphor terminal: Liquid Surface, Falling Letters, Breathing Halo
description:
Why: Phosphor is a quiet terminal. Round 2 adds three small motions that the engine can already draw. Design: /var/tmp/claude/fxlib/redesign2/06.png.

Do:
- Liquid Surface (R2-06-a):
  - What: the waveform is a smooth flowing wave with a few particles riding it.
  - Driver and place: RMS sets amplitude. In the waveform band, not over the text.
  - Subtle: 30 or fewer particles. Reduced: the wave line only, amplitude from RMS.
  - Uses: the existing wave element and emitter.
- Falling Letters (R2-06-b):
  - What: on word commit, faint copies of its letters fall from 12 px above into place over 250 ms with a short vertical glow trail.
  - Driver and place: word-commit; positions from `Scene::word_bounds`. Above the word; the real word is at 70 % ink or more from its first frame.
  - Subtle: copy alpha 20 % or less. Rule: only letters already recognized, never upcoming text. Reduced: no fall, ink rise only.
  - Uses: a canvas with the trail layer; no EG.
- Breathing Halo (R2-06-c):
  - What: a soft arc glow behind the lower text grows and brightens as you speak, like a slow sunrise.
  - Driver and place: smoothed RMS (release 800 ms). Behind the text.
  - Subtle: alpha at the newest line 15 % or less; settles on pause. Reduced: brightness only, no growth.
  - Uses: a gradient shape; no EG.

Files: ~/work/voxtype/src/bin/osd_vo/phosphor.rs; exhibits station/r2_06_a_liquid_surface.rs, r2_06_b_falling_letters.rs and r2_06_c_breathing_halo.rs.

Acceptance:
- Given `--theme phosphor --offline DIR --moment M` for first-word, dictation, pause and final-pass, then first-word +0.12 s shows letters mid-fall; dictation shows a large halo; pause +1 s shows it small.
- Given the same script, when `--envelope` runs, then it passes (newest line: ink 70 % or more, baseline within 3 px, no scale, rotation or blur).
- Given idle-open and recording, then the RD-02 log shows idle at 30 fps or less, CPU under 2 % of a core, GPU p95 under 1 ms at 600x300.
- Given a full dictation and a cancel, then the RD-05 exit check passes.
- Given `--station --only R2-06-a,R2-06-b,R2-06-c`, then each idea plays alone in its own tile.
- Given `--motion reduced-motion`, then the moments show each reduced form above.
- Human check: the maintainer approves a recorded clip of one dictation (`--record`, played with `--preview --replay`).

Tests: Falling copies are gone 250 ms after commit; halo radius is a pure function of RMS; no new engine code is needed. Rendering one moment twice gives identical frames.

title: EG-24 Images and app icons
description:
Size: M. Gap cards: 14.

Why: the delivery receipt says 'typed into konsole' but cannot show the app's icon. There is no image element; `vo_scene::svg` reads single-colour icons into paths only.

Do:
- Image element `Element::image(key, source)` for PNG (the `png` crate) and full-colour SVG (resvg; check the licence of the version you add, recent ones are Apache-2.0 or MIT). Rasterised at logical size times surface scale; cache keyed by (file, pixel size), LRU, at most 8 MB.
- Draw: a textured quad through the EG-02 texture binding, premultiplied and sRGB-correct. CPU first frame (cpu.rs): draw it if already decoded, else skip.
- Icon lookup in the popup, off the render thread: app id (src/osd/target.rs) to `<id>.desktop` or a `StartupWMClass` match in XDG data dirs, its `Icon=`, then the icon theme (kdeglobals `[Icons] Theme`, then hicolor), scalable first. - Given the receipt moment (`--offline --moment` with a fixture icon dir), then the chip draws the icon (golden).
- Given 100 images of 1 MB each, then the cache stays at most 8 MB (unit test).

title: RV-03 Images: no decode per frame, path sources refresh
description:
From the 2026-10-29 review. crates/vo-render/src/image.rs:208-221, crates/vo-scene/src/image.rs:242/69/232. (a) A raster over CACHE_BYTES (8 MB, about 1450x1450) is never stored, and paint() asks ImageCache::raster before its own texture cache, so it decodes on the render thread every frame; check the texture cache first. (b) want comes from to_px's determinant, so an animated layer scale (pop-in) gives a new key every frame: quantise the decode size (for example powers of 2 or 25 % steps) and let the GPU scale. (9) ImageSource::file is keyed by path only and a failure is cached for the life of the process: include the file's mtime and size in the key, and retry failures after a delay (for example 2 s).
Files: crates/vo-scene/src/image.rs, crates/vo-render/src/image.rs.
Acceptance: unit tests: a 2000x2000 image painted 10 frames decodes once; a scale animating 0.8 to 1.0 over 20 frames decodes at most 2 times; a file rewritten at the same path shows new pixels; a missing file created later shows up. Image goldens unchanged.
close_reason: 2bfd510 + clippy fix c49dfd6: painter checks its textures before the decode cache (big rasters decode once); decode size rounds the scale up in 0.25 steps (1/8 below 1) via vo_scene::image::decode_px, shared by GPU painter, CPU first frame and warm; ImageSource::key adds file mtime+size; failures retried after 2 s. Tests: vo-scene 325 pass, vo-render lib 61, gpu_image 5 incl. 3 new; goldens unchanged.

title: EDIT M0.1 KWin focus probe
description:
WHY: Spike: de-risks the design before code is built on it.  Plan id M0.1, v1.

FILES: vo:crates/vo-host-wayland/examples/focus_probe.rs

WHAT TO DO: KWin focus probe. Implement exactly the acceptance below; plan section 6 row M0.1 and the sections it cites are the spec.

REQUIREMENTS (quoted in full):
- R3 (v1): Focus is taken through a separate Overlay layer surface with `on_demand`, mapped with a buffer attached. The visible popup stays at `KeyboardInteractivity::None`. The reason is that KWin's `handleAcceptsFocusChanged` has no branch for the switch back to false, and an `on_demand` popup would steal focus every time it is mapped [V]. This is recorded in `INPUT-MODEL.md`.
- R5 (v1): On a `leave` the popup did not request, the state becomes Detached. "Requested" means a flag the popup sets before it destroys the proxy. Lock screen, output removal, click-away and Alt+Tab all lead to Detached. A single Right Shift tap re-enters editing with the same buffer and caret. Focus is never taken back by itself.
- R27 (v1): On finish, the popup destroys the proxy and reports `ProxyClosed`. The daemon waits until `kdotool getactivewindow` equals the saved id, for at most 500 ms. That is the only handback deadline. If the focus chain picked another window, the daemon calls `kdotool windowactivate <id>` once inside the same 500 ms.
- R40 (v1): From the single-tap decision (release + `double_tap_ms`) to the caret shown takes at most 100 ms [G, measured in M0.1 and M7.2]. With 300 ms that is at most about 400 ms after the release.

ACCEPTANCE (machine-checkable): In nested `kwin_wayland --virtual` on a private, named socket: a mapped, buffered proxy gets `enter` within 50 ms. Destroying it gives focus back to the previous window. Covers two outputs, focus-follows-mouse, the target closed mid-edit, and the lock screen if it can run nested. Also measures the single-surface option. Logs results as a table.

title: RD-05 Exit check: every look ends its show without the motion cap
description:
Why: a look with an endless loop (the Mecha hang) kept a show open until vo's 3 s cap, EXIT_MOTION_MAX in crates/vo/src/app.rs, closed it ("vo: still moving ... closing anyway", printed only live today). With default motion sets (RD-01) and idle motion (RD-02) this gets more likely, so every look needs a check that its show ends by settling, not by the cap.

Do:
- Framework: let an offline run report how it ended, settled at t or cut by the cap, for example a result field from `render_offline_with` or the same "still moving" line on stderr (crates/vo/src/offline.rs, using `Driver::done` and `overdue` from app.rs). No change to live behaviour.
- Popup flag `--exit-check`: runs the scripted dictation of `--offline` without writing PNGs, prints `exit-check: ok <look> settled <s> s after exit` or `exit-check: FAIL <look> still moving <EXIT_MOTION_MAX> s after exit`, and exits 1 on FAIL. It honours `--cancel`, `--motion` and VO_REDUCED_MOTION=1.
- A scripted look switch: a moment `look-switch` in src/bin/osd_vo/moments.rs that steps the look chord mid-dictation (as `step_look` does), so a switch that leaves a loop running is caught. Today `step_look` returns early without a live OSD config and writes $XDG_STATE_HOME/voxtype/osd-look; the moment must work offline with no live config and must never write the saved look (a test checks the state file is untouched). The look beads use this moment for their look-switch checks.
- New script ~/work/voxtype/scripts/osd-vo-looks.sh: for every look in OsdTheme::VO_LOOKS with its defaults, runs `--envelope` and `--exit-check`, each plain, with `--cancel` and with VO_REDUCED_MOTION=1, plus `--exit-check --moment look-switch`. Prints one line per run and a summary; exits 1 when any run fails, naming the look and run.
- Framework justfile: a recipe `osd-looks` that builds the popup (`heavy-build cargo build --release --features osd-vo --bin voxtype-osd-vo` in the fork, like the other `osd-*` recipes) and runs the script. Do not add it to `just all`: that gate must not depend on the fork.
- Run the script on all looks and fix any look that fails, Mecha first. A failure that belongs to an effect not yet ported goes to that look's bead with the log line, not fixed here.

- Given `--exit-check --moment look-switch --theme swiss`, then it exits 0.

title: LAT-5 Forming-word cue: show at once that a word is coming, driven by the live voice level
description:
Why: the maintainer: 'it feels really slow just because there's nothing indicating that there is an active word coming.' The model reports at most every 0.56 s (ghost tail, LAT-1), so the cue must not wait for it: the mic level and voice onsets already reach the popup in real time (the waveform and the sounding/onset channels the looks use).

Do: on by default in every look with live text. At the insertion point (after the last committed word, or after the ghost tail when there is one), draw a word-shaped placeholder that appears within one frame of voice onset and grows with the time spoken since the last word appeared (for example a soft dim bar or dotted blob at x-height, widening about one letter per 80 ms, capped near one long word). It pulses with the voice level, holds still in silence and fades out within about 150 ms after a pause. When ghost or committed words arrive, the placeholder hands over: it shrinks to the remaining unexplained speech or ends, so it never sits on top of real text. When the model's frame signal says a token is near (log10(1-P(blank)) above -2.5 in the latest G step), the placeholder brightens; use that as a bonus, never as the trigger. Each look draws it in its own material (dots in dotmatrix, cyan in karaoke, etc.), subtle, never louder than the text. Reduced motion: a still placeholder that appears and goes, no pulse.

Files: src/bin/osd_vo/model_signals.rs (or a new forming.rs), the look files for material, motion defaults.

Acceptance:
- Latency: on --moment dictation and lookahead, the first frame with the placeholder comes at most 1 frame (<= 34 ms at 30 fps) after the voice onset in the scripted level stream, at both widths, in every look; table per look.
- It never overlaps ghost or committed glyphs (pixel probe) and the envelope check result is unchanged vs --motion no-forming-cue for every look, all 6 runs.
- Silence: in the long-silence moment no placeholder after 150 ms of silence; idle-open CPU within 0.3 % of --motion no-forming-cue.
- Live nested-KWin run on 3 looks at both widths shows the cue at voice onset before any word.
Context: same as LAT-1 (z34h). Rules: /var/tmp/claude/fxlib/swarm/RULES.md.

title: R2-21 Dot matrix: Typewriter Ink, Liquid Glass Flow, Orbital Word Rings

title: EG-11 Fluid simulation core: ink and smoke with memory
description:
Size: L. Gap cards: 6.

Why: ink, smoke and watercolour designs need a flow with memory: dye that curls, drifts and stays where it was pushed. vo has no fluid simulation; noise fields and curl forces on particles do not keep state.

Do:
- A stable-fluids grid on the GPU as a `Sim` of crates/vo-sim (EG-00): velocity and dye fields, semi-Lagrangian advection, a pressure solve with a fixed iteration count (so results do not depend on convergence timing), and vorticity confinement. Fixed 120 Hz tick, snapshots, `state_at(t)`.
- Impulses (pushes) and dye sources are timestamped events with position, direction, radius, colour and strength; the caller records them, the sim never reads live audio.
- Low resolution by default (for example 128x64 for a 600x300 popup); document GPU cost per tick and snapshot memory.
- Output a dye texture (and velocity, for EG-12 smears) that other passes can sample.
- Reduced motion: impulses are ignored; dye sources place still dye.
Files: crates/vo-sim/src/fluid.rs and crates/vo-sim/src/wgsl/fluid.wgsl (new); crates/vo-sim/tests/gpu_fluid.rs (new).

- Given dye injected at one point with one sideways push at t = 0, when read back at t = 2 s, then the dye centre of mass has moved in the push direction by at least 10 cells and the dye shows curl (vorticity magnitude above a documented threshold).
- Given closed boundaries and no sources after t = 0, then total dye at t = 3 s is within 5 % of total dye at t = 0.1 s.
- Given the same events, when sampled through frame steps of 1/144 s and of 1/60 s, then dye textures at equal t are byte-identical; a seek back from 5 s to 2 s equals a fresh run to 2 s.

title: EG-23 Smooth variable-font axes
description:
Size: M. Gap cards: 13.

Why: breathing type uses Roboto Flex instances quantised to steps (`Axes::quantized`: 20 weight, 1 width, 1 degree slant), so a slow loudness ramp jumps.

Do: keep the quantised instances (the font registry never drops fonts) and make the rest continuous on top of the nearest one:
- weight: the remainder becomes glyph edge dilation (`GlyphFx::weight`), calibrated per face so one step of 20 equals the dilation that matches the next instance's ink;
- width: the remainder becomes a horizontal scale in the per-glyph transform (EG-15);
- slant: the remainder becomes skew in the per-glyph transform (EG-15).
- Calibrate once per face at load (measure ink of two neighbouring instances) and cache.
- Reduced motion: unchanged from today.

Files: crates/vo-scene/src/motion/var_axes.rs, crates/vo-scene/src/flow.rs (where word channels apply), crates/vo-scene/tests/variable_font.rs.

Acceptance:
- Given a weight ramp 400 to 600 over 4 s at 60 fps, then the word's ink area per frame (GPU readback) never drops and its largest frame step is at most 1.5x the median step.
- Given a width ramp 95 to 105, then the word width (layout units) never drops and its largest step is at most 1.5x the median.
- Given those ramps, then at most 11 instances are created (no extra memory).
- A reading-line ramp passes `check_scenario` (tracking within 5 %).
- `effect_cost` case `flex-breathing` adds at most 0.05 ms p95 at 600x300, logged.

Tests: unit tests for remainder maths and calibration; the two ramp tests in a GPU test; a recorded demo in text_flow_demo.

Why: several designs want a silk ribbon or cloth strip that twists to show its back and swells with the voice. vo-3d meshes are rigid and uploaded once (mesh.rs); `vo_scene::ribbon` is flat 2D strands.

Do:
- New `crates/vo-3d/src/ribbon3d.rs`: a strip of N segments (default 96) along a 3D centre curve. Closed form, a pure function of t and a level history (`vo_scene::emitter::LevelTrack`): twist and folds are sums of travelling sines, width swells with level. No verlet and no state. Cloth is the same strip made wide; no collisions.
- mesh.rs: add a `uv` attribute to `Vertex` (zero in the existing builders) and `Renderer3d::update_mesh` that rewrites a mesh's vertices each frame (same count, `queue.write_buffer`).
- wgsl/mesh.wgsl: two-sided shading (front and back colour by `front_facing`), fine fibre lines along the length from uv, no culling for ribbons.
- Reduced motion: the rest pose; level changes brightness only.
- Demo `crates/vo-3d/examples/ribbon_demo.rs` with a contact sheet and `--bench`, like hero_demo.

Files: crates/vo-3d/src/ribbon3d.rs (new), crates/vo-3d/src/mesh.rs, crates/vo-3d/src/wgsl/mesh.wgsl.

Acceptance:
- Given twist amplitude 180 degrees, when rendered at the pose where it passes 90 degrees, then back-colour pixels are at least 10 % of ribbon pixels.
- Given level 0 and level 1, then mean strip width at level 1 is at least 1.3x (CPU test on vertices).
- Given t sampled after a forward run and after a random-order run, then the vertices are bit-identical.
- `ribbon_demo --bench` at 600x300: p95 GPU time of one ribbon at most 0.3 ms, logged in the commit message. Without timestamp queries it prints that and exits 0.
- `just test-gpu` passes; existing vo-3d goldens unchanged.

Tests: unit tests for width, twist, purity; GPU goldens (crates/vo-3d/tests/goldens) at scale 1 and 1.5, a light background, and reduced motion. The CPU first frame (vo-render cpu.rs) skips GPU items: assert the demo's first CPU frame does not panic.

Shared rules: read CLAUDE.md in both repos first. Framework: ~/work/voxtype-osd-gpu (main). Popup: ~/work/voxtype (branch voxtype-onnx-isolation, shared checkout: commit with a pathspec, never switch branch, reset or rebase). Builds and tests through `heavy-build` (load the heavy-build skill). Reserve files with agent mail. One bead, one or more commits, never amend. Never open a window on the real display (`--offline`, `--envelope`, `vo-preview`, or a nested `kwin_wayland --virtual`). Every animation stays a pure function of time plus recorded events (replayable); a simulation steps at a fixed tick with snapshots. Keep the reading-line envelope, the GPU budget (1 ms per frame p95 at 600x300) and a reduced-motion form. Add a vo-preview demo or station exhibit that shows the new ability. Plan: docs/ENGINE-GAPS-PLAN.md. Gallery (gap cards and every design): https://claude.ai/artifact/E3J8iqQE9aAn7XdXQYjgeB.
close_reason: Ribbon3d + RibbonItem (closed-form twist/fold/swell, reduced motion), Vertex uv, Renderer3d::update_mesh, Source3d::vertices, two-sided mesh shader with back colour and fibres, ribbon_demo with --bench (p95 0.023 ms silk, 0.026 ms cloth at 600x300), goldens. Commits 098df73, 87b7cbd.

title: RV-05 Text field on wide targets and the liquid painter flag
description:
From the 2026-10-29 review. (7) crates/vo-render/src/text_field.rs:38 and 176: the field is clamped to 3584 texels wide but coverage is drawn at scale/downscale, so ink past that column is missing; raise the downscale for wide targets so the whole surface fits. Also crates/vo-scene/src/motion/liquid.rs PAINTER is a process-wide flag: if set while a renderer or the CPU first frame has no glyph_fx painter, words off the reading line vanish for 0.36 s; decide per renderer (or the CPU path draws the palimpsest).
Files: crates/vo-render/src/text_field.rs, crates/vo-scene/src/motion/liquid.rs, crates/vo-render/src/cpu.rs (fallback only).
Acceptance: text_dist test on a 7680 px target finds ink at x=7000; a CPU first-frame test during a liquid revision shows the word; existing gpu_text_field and gpu_liquid_revision tests pass.

title: COR-2 Correction matcher: find the span a respoken phrase replaces
description:

Given the text frozen at correction start (last ~40 timed words) and the correction words, score runs of k words (k = n +- 2) by normalised phonetic edit distance (Double Metaphone or consonant skeleton) plus a small recency cost; accept if score < 0.45 and it beats the runner-up span by >= 0.1. description:

description:

title: EG-04 Layer blur and frosted shapes
description:
Size: M. Gap cards: 11.

Why: vo has no blur of a layer or of what is under a shape; only glyph edge softening, bloom and motion blur. Depth-stack sheets, out-of-focus far words and soft reflections need a real blur.

Do:
- Layer blur: a separable blur (dual Kawase or two-pass Gaussian, the implementer picks by measured cost) on an offscreen layer, with an animatable radius (a new animatable property on layers; pick a name that does not clash with the text-effect blur).
- Frost on shapes: a shape option that blurs its backdrop (EG-01) inside the shape's outline, so a sheet frosts the lines behind it.
- Radius 0 costs nothing (no pass). The radius follows the quality tier (`vo_render::Quality`, VO_QUALITY): `minimal` draws no blur.
- Reduced motion: the radius does not animate (it jumps to its target).
- Never on the newest (reading) line: the envelope forbids blur there; frost behind it is fine.
- Add effect_cost cases `layer blur r8` and `frost r8`.

Acceptance:
- Given a single white pixel blurred at radius 4, then the result is symmetric and sums to the input within 1/255 per channel (CPU readback in a GPU test).
- Given a demo of three depth-stack sheets with frost over two older lines, when rendered offscreen, then it matches a new golden in crates/vo-render/tests/gpu_blur.rs, at scale 1 and 1.5.
- Given radius 0, then output equals the unblurred layer byte for byte, and effect_cost shows no added pass.
- Given effect_cost at 600x300, then each blur case adds under 2 ms, and the depth-stack demo stays under 1 ms p95 for the whole frame; numbers in the commit message.
- Given the same scene at the same t twice, then frames are byte-identical.
Tests: gpu_blur.rs goldens and the impulse test; `just test`, `just test-gpu`, `just budget` exit 0; a vo-preview demo of frosted sheets.

title: EG-07 Frosted glass looks use KDE blur-behind, shaped to the outline
description:
Size: M. Gap cards: 1, 10.

Why: frosted glass looks need the desktop blurred behind them, and the maintainer chose compositor blur over screen capture. vo can already ask KWin to blur (ext-background-effect, crates/vo-host-wayland/src/blur.rs), and `DisplayList::blur_region` (crates/vo-scene/src/glass.rs) already steps rounded corners. But only axis-aligned rounded-rect glass gets a region, rotated glass gets its bounding box, and the popup never turns blur on.

Do:
- Blur region from any outline: chamfers, notches, filled paths and the shapes EG-06 gives glass, and rotated or tilted layers. Step the region per row of physical pixels along slanted and curved edges, as `blur_rects` does for corners, so no blur spills past the outline. Cap the rect count (for example 256) by merging rows; document the cap.
- A non-glass translucent element can also ask for blur behind its outline.
- When the compositor has no blur (`caps.backdrop_blur` false), the look draws its plain tint and logs once.
- One popup helper in ~/work/voxtype src/bin/osd_vo/kit.rs that a look calls to turn blur-behind on for its panel outline. Do not edit look files: each look adopts it in its own look or R2 bead.
Files: crates/vo-scene/src/glass.rs (region from outlines), crates/vo-host-wayland/src/blur.rs (only if the region path needs it); src/bin/osd_vo/kit.rs in the popup.

Acceptance:
- Given a chamfered octagon (chamfer 12 px) at scale 1 and 1.25, then a unit test shows every region rect lies inside the outline (no spill beyond 1 physical px) and the rects cover at least 97 % of its area, with at most the documented rect count.
- Given a card rotated 15 degrees, then the same two checks hold.
- Given a rounded rect, then the region equals today's `blur_rects` output.
- Given a nested `kwin_wayland --virtual` with a sharp checkerboard behind a demo surface with an octagon glass (a vo example, or `blur_probe` extended), when a screenshot is taken (spectacle needs KWIN_WAYLAND_NO_PERMISSION_CHECKS=1), then pixels outside the outline equal the checkerboard, and pixel variance inside is at most half of outside.
- Given a compositor without blur, then the demo draws and logs "no compositor blur" once.
Tests: the unit tests in crates/vo-scene; the nested KWin screenshot check as a script or test with its numbers logged; `just test` and `just lint` exit 0; the kit.rs helper unit-tested for its region on the swiss panel.

title: particles: the finish and done lifts move the reading line (envelope baseline)
description:
Found in RD-09 (fgaw). Popup 57c4c88, framework aa968ff.

What is drawn: when particles enters Finishing (stop or cancel), the words move up FINISH_LIFT (14 design px) to make room for the progress bar; at Done they move up DONE_LIFT (30). Both are deliberate (particles.rs, consts FINISH_LIFT and DONE_LIFT, card_h). The newest line moves with them, so --envelope reports a baseline breach on the reading line.

Numbers, --envelope --motion none at 30 fps (600 px / empty config):
- plain: baseline 105x / 79x, worst 14.00 / 9.33 px (word 53 at 6.533 s, frame 196: the stop)
- --cancel: baseline 219x / 195x, worst 14.00 / 9.33 px (word 25 at 3.033 s, frame 91: the cancel)
- VO_REDUCED_MOTION=1: baseline 26x, worst 14.00 / 9.33 px (word 53 at 6.433 s)
Default motion at 10 fps: plain 39x, reduced 4x, worst 14.00 px. No motion feature causes it: every --motion no-X and --motion X run gives the same numbers.

Decision for the maintainer: (a) keep the lift and accept the breach at the phase change, (b) grow the card downward by the bar's room instead, so the words stay put (card 14 px taller while finishing), or (c) lift only the older lines and keep the newest line in place.
close_reason: particles keeps the words where they were read and grows the card down at finish and done (popup c21257a). --motion none, 6 runs: ok at both widths (before: baseline 14.00 px at 600, 9.33 px empty).

title: EG-27 Particles drawn as tiny letters
description:

- Reduced motion: letters fade in place, no travel.

- Given a seek back, then the frame equals a fresh run (bytes).

title: Swiss look: subtle idle motion that makes it feel alive
description:
Add 3 subtle always-on motions to the Swiss look, inside the RD-02 policy, so it feels alive while open. The maintainer wants calm, not flashy.

Do:
- Accent hairline shimmer: a 60 px soft highlight (+20 % lightness) runs along the top accent hairline once every 8 s, 1.2 s per pass.
- Recording dot breathes: opacity 0.7 to 1.0 on a 2.4 s cycle, only while listening.
- Timer colon softens: the elapsed-time colon dims to 50 % for 250 ms at each whole second.
- Run through the RD-02 paced idle path at its capped rate, only while the popup is open; stop at once on exit and on a look switch. Nothing changes the glyphs of the newest line.
- Reduced motion (`reduced-motion` or VO_REDUCED_MOTION=1): all of them off, the look still.
Files: src/bin/osd_vo/swiss_look.rs (after dqb moves it out of voxtype_osd_vo.rs).

Acceptance (B = target/release/voxtype-osd-vo built through heavy-build with `--features osd-vo`; D = a new empty folder):
- Given swiss open with no speech, when the RD-02 per-look measurement runs, then idle frames stay at or under the capped rate. CPU and GPU stay under the RD-02 budget (proposed: 2 % of one core, 1 ms GPU per frame at 600x300).
- Given `B --theme swiss --offline D --moment long-silence`, when two idle-tail frames 1 s apart are compared (`compare -metric AE`), then some panel pixels differ and none inside the newest line's box (newest_line_centre +/- half a line).
- Given the same run with VO_REDUCED_MOTION=1, then those two frames are identical.
- Given done and cancel (`--offline D --cancel`), then the run exits 0 and no "still moving" in stderr.
- Given the look chord steps away while idle, then the old idle loops stop in that frame.
- `B --theme swiss --envelope` adds no breach with the idle motion on.
Tests: the checks above; the RD-02 number for this look goes in docs/REDESIGN-PLAN.md.

description:

title: R2-19 Aurora mesh: Prismatic Lens, Luminous Ink, Magnetic Type
description:
Why: Aurora mesh is soft colour. Round 2 adds caustics on the rim, dye behind the text and field lines. Design: /var/tmp/claude/fxlib/redesign2/19.png.

Do:
- Prismatic Lens (R2-19-a):
  - What: soft rainbow caustics flow around the panel rim.
  - Driver and place: RMS sets flow speed. Panel rim; the text stays crisp.
  - Rule: the design refracts the background; there is no screen capture, so caustics are procedural and highlights come from EG-21. Reduced: still caustics.
  - Uses: a caustic material; EG-21.
- Luminous Ink (R2-19-b):
  - What: dye blooms behind the text and thins out within 2 s of silence.
  - Driver and place: RMS and word-commit. Behind the text; alpha at the newest line 20 % or less.
  - Reduced: still wash.
  - Uses: EG-11, EG-12.
- Magnetic Type (R2-19-c):
  - What: faint field lines behind the text curve with the voice; older lines may follow the curve by 6 px or less per letter.
  - Driver and place: RMS. Background and older lines; the newest line stays flat.
  - Subtle: line alpha 12 % or less. Reduced: straight lines, no letter offsets.
  - Uses: a material; EG-15, EG-16 for older lines.

Files: the aurora look file RD-03 creates in ~/work/voxtype/src/bin/osd_vo/; exhibits station/r2_19_a_prismatic_lens.rs, r2_19_b_luminous_ink.rs and r2_19_c_magnetic_type.rs.

Acceptance:
- Given `--theme aurora --offline DIR --moment M` for first-word, dictation, pause and final-pass, then dictation shows bright caustics and curved lines with older text on the curve; pause +2 s shows little dye.
- Given the same script, when `--envelope` runs, then it passes (newest line: ink 70 % or more, baseline within 3 px, no scale, rotation or blur).
- Given idle-open and recording, then the RD-02 log shows idle at 30 fps or less, CPU under 2 % of a core, GPU p95 under 1 ms at 600x300.
- Given a full dictation and a cancel, then the RD-05 exit check passes.
- Given `--station --only R2-19-a,R2-19-b,R2-19-c`, then each idea plays alone in its own tile.
- Given `--motion reduced-motion`, then the moments show each reduced form above.
- Human check: the maintainer approves a recorded clip of one dictation (`--record`, played with `--preview --replay`).

Tests: Newest-line letters have zero offset and rotation; older-line offsets stay within 6 px; dye replays to the same snapshot. Rendering one moment twice gives identical frames.

title: EG-05 Refracting glass: lenses, prisms and slabs bend what is under them
description:
Size: L. Gap cards: 4.

Why: glass today tints, bevels and rims, but reads no texture, so nothing under it bends. Lenses, prisms and glass slabs in the designs must refract what is under them (the popup's own drawing, never the desktop).

Do:
- Glass samples its backdrop (EG-01, through the texture path of EG-02) at an offset from its own surface normal. The normal comes from the shape's SDF (EG-06 gives glass any outline) or from a lens profile.
- Options: magnification, and per-channel dispersion (red, green and blue sampled at different offsets) for rainbow edges.
- Presets: lens disc, prism, thick slab, bubble with thin-film iridescence. Each has a dark and a light form (`Renderer::set_light`, VO_LIGHT=1), and text on or under it keeps passing `Glass::contrast` (the AX01 check).
- Reduced motion: refraction stays (it is not motion); any animated wobble or sheen stops.
- Add effect_cost cases `glass lens` and `glass prism`.
Files: crates/vo-render/src/glass.rs, wgsl/glass.wgsl; crates/vo-scene/src/glass.rs (presets and API).

Acceptance:
- Given a lens disc at magnification 1.5 over a HUD ring with 12 ticks, when rendered offscreen, then the tick spacing under the lens centre is 1.5 times the spacing outside (measured on readback within 1 px), and it matches a new golden in crates/vo-render/tests/gpu_glass_refract.rs.
- Given a prism over a white beam with dispersion on, then the red and blue edges of the beam's exit land at least 2 px apart, in opposite directions from green.
- Given dispersion 0 and magnification 1 with a flat profile, then output under the glass equals plain glass over the same backdrop.
- Given light mode and dark mode, then each preset with text over it passes the AX01 contrast check (`Glass::contrast`) at the threshold the existing glass tests use.
- Given effect_cost at 600x300, then each case adds under 2 ms; numbers in the commit message.
Tests: gpu_glass_refract.rs goldens and the two readback checks; existing glass goldens unchanged; `just test`, `just test-gpu`, `just budget` exit 0; a demo in crates/vo/examples/glass_demo showing the four presets.

- Living Glass (R2-02-a):
  - What: a glass lens over the mic ring bends the ring and waveform under it; a closed-form ripple in the lens shader follows the voice.
  - Driver and place: RMS for ripple height. Over the mic ring only, away from the text.
  - Subtle: offset 3 px or less; highlights from EG-21. Reduced: still lens.
  - Uses: EG-05 (with EG-01, EG-02, EG-06), EG-21. Rule: the lens bends only layers vo drew, never desktop pixels.
- Particle Orbit (R2-02-b):
  - What: 300 or fewer particles orbit the mic, tightening and brightening as you speak and loosening on pause.
  - Driver and place: RMS drives ring pull and swirl speed. Around the ring, outside the text.
  - Subtle: particle alpha 40 % or less. Reduced: a still dotted ring whose brightness follows RMS.
  - Uses: the existing particles (swirl, ring pull, audio forces); no EG.
- Typewriter Approach (R2-02-c):
  - What: on word commit, 2 to 4 faint copies of its letters glide in along arcs around the ring and merge into the word within 300 ms.
  - Driver and place: word-commit; target from `Scene::word_bounds`. Around the ring and outside the newest line; the real word is at 70 % ink or more from its first frame.
  - Subtle: copy alpha 25 % or less. Reduced: no copies, ink rise only.
  - Uses: EG-15 and EG-16 for letters turned along the arc.

Files: ~/work/voxtype/src/bin/osd_vo/jarvis.rs; exhibits station/r2_02_a_living_glass.rs, r2_02_b_particle_orbit.rs and r2_02_c_typewriter_approach.rs.

title: EG-18 Soft shadows in 3D
description:
Size: M. Gap cards: 9.

Why: typebars, platens and other meshes float without contact shadows. vo-3d has one key light and no shadows.

Do:
- New `crates/vo-3d/src/shadow.rs`: a shadow map for the directional key light, 512x512 Depth16 by default (512 KB), fit to the meshes' bounds each frame. Soft edges by PCF (Poisson disc, 8 to 16 taps) with a `softness` setting in pixels.
- `Frame3d` gets `shadows: Option<Shadows { softness, size }>`. `None` draws exactly as today.
- Casters: meshes. Receivers: the floor (floor.wgsl) and meshes (mesh.wgsl). The raymarched hero neither casts nor receives (out of scope).
- Stateless: rebuilt from the current pose each frame, so replay is exact.
- Demo `crates/vo-3d/examples/shadow_demo.rs`: a box and a torus over the floor, contact sheet and `--bench`.

Files: crates/vo-3d/src/shadow.rs (new), crates/vo-3d/src/render.rs, crates/vo-3d/src/wgsl/mesh.wgsl and floor.wgsl.

Acceptance:
- Given `shadows: None`, then every existing vo-3d golden is unchanged.
- Given a box 40 px above the floor, then the floor under it is at least 30 % darker than open floor, and the edge goes from 10 % to 90 % of that darkening over at least 3 px (scanline check).
- `shadow_demo --bench` at 600x300: shadows add at most 0.25 ms p95, logged in the commit message. No timestamps: print and exit 0.

title: Radial look: subtle idle motion that makes it feel alive
description:
Add 3 subtle always-on motions to the Radial look, inside the RD-02 policy, so it feels alive while open. The maintainer wants calm, not flashy.

Do:
- Spectrum ring turns: 6 degrees per second (one turn a minute).
- Tick shimmer: one tick at a time brightens 30 % for 300 ms, every 0.5 to 1.5 s.
- Centre glow breathes: 85 % to 100 % on a 4 s cycle.
- Run through the RD-02 paced idle path at its capped rate, only while the popup is open; stop at once on exit and on a look switch. Nothing changes the glyphs of the newest line.
- Reduced motion (`reduced-motion` or VO_REDUCED_MOTION=1): all of them off, the look still.

title: ASR-02 parakeet-rs: keep the per-step model signals it already computes
description:
Why: each decoder call computes a 1025-way distribution and drops everything but the emitted token's p.

Do (fork branch voxtype-signals, parakeet_unified.rs around :480-536):
- Per decoder call: one log-softmax; keep top-k (id, logp) with k = 5, logp_blank, entropy (NeMo-style Tsallis alpha 0.33 with exp normalisation, and plain Shannon), top-2 margin. Expose `token_details()` beside `token_confidences()`.
- Per blank frame: push (abs_frame, log10(1 - P(blank)), top-3 non-blank) into a `frame_signals()` list.
- No change to the emitted tokens or text.
Files: src/parakeet_unified.rs (+ tests in that crate).

Acceptance:
- Unit test or example: on one fixture wav, the transcript and token frames are byte-identical to before.
- The per-frame levels on the fixture match probe_stream.py's dump (probe/run_base/<clip>_steps.json) within 1e-3 in log10.
- Added cost per step under 1 ms (logged).

Context: research page https://claude.ai/artifact/PNRjafNcUxBTuTuqvci9uq; scripts, data and plots in /var/tmp/claude/asr-internals/ (probe_stream.py is a Python port of the parakeet-rs unified loop that reproduces the offline transcripts exactly; surgery.py exports encoder layers; sweep.py the window sweep). Live model: parakeet-unified-en-0.6b-int8, plain RNN-T, 1025-way joint (blank = 1024), steps every 0.56 s over a window of 5.6 s left + 0.56 s chunk + 0.56 s right context, greedy, append-only; median commit wait 0.96 s. parakeet-rs fork: github.com/oysteinkrog/parakeet-rs branch voxtype-confidence (f250ecc), checked out in ~/src/parakeet-rs; never edit there: add a worktree under /var/tmp/claude/ on a new branch voxtype-signals off voxtype-confidence, commit there, and the lead pushes it and moves voxtype's [patch] in Cargo.toml to a rev. voxtype code: ~/work/voxtype (worker.rs, subprocess.rs, revisions.rs, osd/live.rs, the popup). title: RV-01 Blur region: clip to the surface and stop the per-sample n-squared cost
description:
From the 2026-10-29 review of 5a8765c..34cfe55. crates/vo-scene/src/glass.rs rows() (653-661, called at 789/804; live.rs:324 calls it every sample, kept frames too). A glass or blur_behind outline on a warped/rotated layer with a point near the eye plane gives y around 1e6 unclipped; ymax.ceil() as i32 saturates and the band loop runs one band per logical pixel with a full cross() over every point: the UI thread stalls. Also a ~1000-point wavy outline costs O(n^2 log n) per sample.
Do: clip the outline (or the y range) to the surface rect before rasterising; compute the region only when the outline or layer transform changed (cache by a key that covers every input); keep EG-07's outputs identical for normal panels.
Files: crates/vo-scene/src/glass.rs, crates/vo/src/live.rs (call site only).
Acceptance: unit test with a point at y=1e7 returns in under 5 ms with all rects inside the surface; a 1000-point wavy outline: region built once over 60 unchanged samples (counter); EG-07 unit tests unchanged.

title: EG-00 vo-sim crate: fixed-tick simulations that replay
description:
Size: S. Why: the water (EG-09) and fluid (EG-11) simulations need the same base: a grid that steps at a fixed tick and can be rebuilt at any time t. One bead makes the crate, so the two lanes do not both create it.

Do:
- New crate crates/vo-sim (the workspace takes crates/* already; add it to `just all` only if a recipe needs it). A small `Sim` trait: fixed tick (120 Hz, like the particles), seeded events with timestamps (drops, pushes, dye), `step`, `snapshot`, `restore`, and `state_at(t)` that restores the nearest snapshot at or before t and steps forward. Follow the seek pattern of crates/vo-render/src/particles.rs (`Particles::snapshot`).
- Events between ticks apply at the first tick at or after their time, so the state at t depends only on t and the event list, never on how often frames were drawn.
- Snapshot policy: one every N ticks (default 1 s), with a memory cap; document both and the cost of a seek.
- A reference sim: a dot of value that diffuses on a small grid (for example 64x32). It may run on the CPU so its tests run in `just test`; the trait must not assume the CPU, since EG-09 and EG-11 run on the GPU.
Files: crates/vo-sim/Cargo.toml, crates/vo-sim/src/lib.rs, crates/vo-sim/src/snapshot.rs, crates/vo-sim/src/reference.rs (all new).

Acceptance:
- Given the reference sim with three timed events, when it is sampled at the same t through frame steps of 1/144 s and of 1/60 s, then the two states are byte-identical.
- Given a run to t = 5 s and a seek back to t = 2.3 s, then the state equals a fresh run to 2.3 s, byte for byte.
- Given an event at t = 1.004 s, then it applies at tick 121 (the first tick at or after it) in both frame schedules.
- Given 60 s of run time, then snapshot memory stays under the documented cap.
- Given `just test` and `just lint`, then both exit 0.
Tests: unit tests for the four cases above in crates/vo-sim; log seek time from 0 to 60 s in the test output.

title: EG-06 Glass on any outline and on tilted layers
